key_insight: Laser remelting densified detonation-sprayed NiCrFeBSiC coatings, increasing hardness and adhesion while reducing specific wear rate by 49.5%.
engineering_relevance: Combining detonation spraying with laser remelting shows promise for wear-resistant nickel-based protection of mechanical and power-engineering components.
method: Detonation-spray NiCrFeBSiC onto AISI 321 stainless steel, then laser-remelt.
Compare microstructure and phases using SEM, EDS, and XRD.
Evaluate indentation properties, adhesion, friction, wear, and electrochemical corrosion.
evidence_signal: Before/after testing showed porosity falling from 0.306% to 0.15%, hardness rising from 1049.1 to 1206.1 HV, and average friction coefficient decreasing from 0.535 to 0.409.
watch_item: Corrosion current density decreased by only about 3%, so the substantial wear improvement should not be interpreted as a comparable corrosion-resistance gain.
paper_title: Effect of Laser Remelting on the Microstructure, Mechanical and Tribological Properties of Detonation-Sprayed NiCrFeBSiC Coatings for Mechanical Engineering Applications
